invariants.evidence: No second SWAP kernel or alternate application kernel is introduced.
The frozen binding is runtime/coupler provenance; kernel I/O remains absent.
Accepted water mass, donor-temperature provenance, physical state, and energy result remain separate categories.
External donor bindings are candidate-scoped provenance, not persistent per-column physical state.
Future binding storage is explicitly worker/job/candidate scoped and cheaply disposable on retry.
Contract allows compact arrays, pools, and batched storage despite logical sample-oriented API.
Lineage prevents rejected, rolled-back, superseded, or stale candidate bindings from crossing transaction boundaries.
Bindings can be discarded and rebuilt without a physical re-solve; no donor-temperature history is required.
Binding is tied to generic accepted sample intervals and ordinals, with no day/month/year semantics.
No midnight or daily-window assumption is introduced; coupling windows remain generic.
External thermal provenance is designed as supplemental coupling/runtime functionality with explicit transactional lineage.
Groundwater H/q interface authority remains byte-identical and is not redefined by energy binding.
Accepted water remains the sole mass authority; thermal binding cannot alter, duplicate, or rebook water.
No change to interface sensitivity ownership or production response-tangent contracts.
No extra physical SWAP or groundwater solve is authorized to obtain donor temperature.
Optional bindings are compact and can be batched; no per-column heavy solver object is required.
No MODFLOW-cell or tile fraction is represented in the SWAP thermal binding contract.
Deep-vadose provenance remains external; SWAP need not know whether incoming water passed through a transfer zone.
Thermal metadata neither creates nor destroys stored water and does not alter component-transfer mass accounting.
Binding is independent of Full Richards, RossFast, coarse Richards, or any soil-water solver implementation.
Existing EB-I04/I14/I15 sensible-enthalpy physics/accounting is reused; no duplicate process physics is introduced.
No HeadCalc or soil-water solver internal is exposed or required for external donor binding.
External donor provenance is a composition/input contract, not a solver-performance policy that changes physics.
Missing or invalid thermal provenance fails closed for energy without causing unbounded hydrologic retries or compromising mass.
Reference hydrology and thermal-carrier behavior are unchanged in this design-only workunit.
Contract requires explicit missing/invalid/stale/duplicate binding outcomes rather than silent fallback.
External thermal provenance incurs storage/work only when the optional path and applicable inflow samples are active.
Runtime/coupler owns source composition and provides an opaque source-agnostic binding; SWAP does not know component topology.
No implicit .swp, MODFLOW, daily, midnight, local-temperature, T_ref, zero, or interval-only donor assumption is permitted.
This audit explicitly evaluates all 30 architecture invariants and the qualification gate requires exact IDs 1..30.
